solutions.check: 31 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Press often played with by Trump

definitions.meaning: the household sense: smoothing creases out of a shirt
a golf club; Trump is a keen golfer who owns many courses

explanation.surface: The press as a toy Trump likes to play with.
explanation.walkthrough: "Press" wants to be the newspapers Trump spars with; it is the verb for smoothing clothes, and the second half points to his golf bag.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it is a plain synonym of press, smoothing cloth with heat; as a noun it is a golf club, and Trump plays constantly.

clue.text: Conservatives unhappy with 9/18's editorial craft?

definitions.note: the definition works in context: the Conservatives are unhappy with 9/18's leadership

parts.note: a newspaper's leader is its editorial
a ship is a sea craft

explanation.surface: Tory grumbling about Kemi Badenoch, framed as a dig at her newspaper skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 9/18 is KEMI BADENOCH, the answer to the linked clue elsewhere in this grid, then Conservative leader. "Editorial craft" reads as journalism but splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: What Conservatives were unhappy with was Badenoch's running of the party, her leadership.

clue.text: Woeful tale of bastards (Conservative)

parts.note: SOB, short for son of a bitch, is an insult like bastard
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative party

explanation.surface: A satirist's summary of a sad saga involving the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: SOB stands for son of a bitch, so it can stand in for bastard; the brackets only set off the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a tale of woe told to win sympathy.

clue.text: "Yen's in shit" — China

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow

parts.note: the last two letters of shit run on into the first two of China

explanation.surface: A crude quote about a currency in trouble, attributed to China.
explanation.walkthrough: "Yen" looks like Japanese money but is the definition, meaning a longing; the quotation marks and dash are there only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a yen and an itch are both a restless longing for something.

clue.text: A craving to snap: "Dom is a pain!"

indicators.note: to snap is to break, so the quoted complaint is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone is driven to snap by an irritating man called Dom, the quote mimicking a fed-up colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words are the fodder: rearrange DOMISAPAIN after 'snap'. Dom also hints at Dominic Cummings, a frequent Private Eye target.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipsomania is an uncontrollable craving for alcohol, so it is a craving of a particular kind.

clue.text: see 14ac.
DRILL AROUND GREENLAND'S TIP — one of Trump's preoccupations

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the drilling tool goes about the tip letter

parts.note: a borer is a drill, a tool for making holes
the tip of Greenland is its end letter

explanation.surface: A shouted plan to drill round the end of Greenland, an island Trump keeps eyeing.
explanation.walkthrough: BORER (a drill) goes 'AROUND' D, the last letter of Greenland.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump has repeatedly fixated on the US southern frontier and his border wall, so a border is one of his obsessions.

clue.text: Like the politician's reductive announcements of crunch measure?

definitions.meaning: politicians reduce policy to soundbites, short and easily swallowed
a crunch is one chomp, so this is the amount taken in one mouthful

explanation.surface: A jab at politicians who boil a crisis policy down to slogans.
explanation.walkthrough: "Crunch measure" reads as an emergency policy at a crunch point; the question mark flags that it means the amount of one mouthful.
explanation.definitionFit: It means small and easy to take in, as soundbites are, and literally the size of one mouthful.

clue.text: Guiding principle has Democrat on notice perhaps around Republican

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the remaining letters follow the Democrat letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the reworked letters sit round the Republican letter
perhaps signals that the word notice is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A political doctrine where the Democrats keep a wary eye on a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges notice into OCTINE, which goes 'around' R, all after D.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or a principle that guides policy, such as the Monroe Doctrine.

clue.text: (& 18dn.) Demonic Bake-off host, at first a staunch right-winger

indicators.note: gone off, spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: only the first letter of host

parts.note: the first letter of host

explanation.surface: A sinister presenter of The Great British Bake Off revealed as a hardline conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a TV baking contest, so "Bake-off host" looks like a presenter; the hyphen hides the anagram signal "off". Kemi Badenoch became Conservative leader in 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Kemi Badenoch is a Conservative politician on the right of her party.

clue.text: Campish habit?

definitions.meaning: not flamboyant but like a camp, where tents stand
a habit is a garment, as a nun wears

explanation.surface: A flamboyant manner or mannerism.
explanation.walkthrough: "Campish" wants to mean theatrical; it means tent-like. "Habit" wants to be a routine; it is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent dress is a loose, wide dress that hangs like a tent.

clue.text: A strict believer in truth as 'idiotic'

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: the last letter of truth, all of as, and the first two of idiotic

explanation.surface: A sceptic sneering that a devout believer's truth is idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks round 'idiotic' make it look like a sneer being reported; they are only surface, and the answer runs across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a member of a strictly observant Jewish movement.

clue.text: Knocked back one adult drink like a military type

indicators.note: turned back to front, as a drink is knocked back

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
A is the film rating for adult
rum is a drink
as means like

explanation.surface: Someone downing a drink like a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: "Knocked back" reads as drinking, which fits the rum, but it turns the whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's old warrior class.

clue.text: Putin's thing: breaking arms limit, crushing independence

indicators.note: the letters of arms limit break up
the rearranged letters squeeze I inside them

parts.note: these letters rearranged
I is the abbreviation for independence

explanation.surface: Putin tearing up an arms treaty and trampling on a nation's independence.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word of the surface is real-world news about Russia, which makes the anagram hard to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Militarism, the glorification of military power, is Putin's thing.

clue.text: (& 6dn./22dn.) Shroud to go here? Never!

definitions.meaning: a shroud is laid over a corpse
the phrase for a flat refusal

explanation.surface: Someone refusing outright a plan to wrap them in a shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half takes the idiom literally: where does a shroud go? Over a corpse, your own.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic way of saying never, and literally where a shroud is laid.

clue.text: Ex-president's ire seen to explode on taking question

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the ex-president is the answer

indicators.note: taking means holding within, so the scrambled letters take the question word inside
letters that explode are blown apart and land in a new order

parts.note: how is a question word

explanation.surface: A former US leader's anger is seen to boil over when he is quizzed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to explode' rearranges IRE SEEN into EISENER, and 'taking' puts HOW inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was the 34th President of the United States, serving 1953 to 1961.

clue.text: A PM told off on accepting Cyclops as moderator

indicators.note: on accepting means after taking in, so the scrambled letters take the setter's letter inside
told off here means the letters of told are set off, knocked out of order

parts.note: the setter Cyclops refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A prime minister is reprimanded for appointing the satirist Cyclops as a mediator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges A PM TOLD into DPLOMAT, and 'on accepting' puts I (the setter, Cyclops) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is someone tactful who smooths over disputes, so they act as a go-between or moderator.

clue.text: Nothing gained by "hot and cold" Truss's comeback?

indicators.note: coming back means read in reverse

parts.note: H for hot, as on a tap
C for cold, as on a tap
Liz Truss, briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022

explanation.surface: A jibe that nothing would come of a political comeback by the erratic Liz Truss.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hot and cold" suggests blowing hot and cold, fickleness; it is just the two tap letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from American slang meaning zero, nothing at all.

clue.text: Bribe disheartened bobby to trap union leader

indicators.note: to lose heart is to lose the centre, so the word keeps only its outside letters
the outer letters close round the next one like a trap

parts.note: bobby without its middle

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the first letter of union

parts.note: the first letter of union

explanation.surface: A corrupt police officer planning to catch a trade union boss.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British police officer, but only the outside of the word is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to pay off an official is to bribe them.

clue.text: See 9dn.
Wrong robots etc for the occupied territory

parts.note: a wrong is a sin
AI, artificial intelligence, covers robots and the like

explanation.surface: A complaint that using robots in an occupied territory is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: "Wrong" looks like an instruction to rearrange robots; it is a noun meaning sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel occupied the Sinai peninsula from 1967 until 1982.

clue.text: Is put off by dickhead's rash

indicators.note: by means next to, so the head letter follows the jumbled letters
off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters of is put are rearranged

parts.note: the head of the word dick is its first letter; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by an idiot's hasty behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges IS PUT into STUPI, and 'by' sets the head of dick, D, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid and rash both describe acting foolishly without thinking things through.

clue.text: Appreciative communication from cooler: "Bloke's sound"

parts.note: a fan cools a room

indicators.note: the word as heard, not spelt

parts.note: a bloke is a man, a male

explanation.surface: A note of thanks from someone assuring you a man is dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sound" reads as the adjective, reliable; it signals a homophone. Bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Fan mail is letters of admiration sent to a celebrity.

clue.text: Goes limp — Labour leader quits, so swells

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so the first letter of Labour

parts.note: to flop is to go limp

indicators.note: to quit is to leave, so that letter departs

parts.note: the first letter of Labour, removed

explanation.surface: A political sketch: the Labour leader resigns, and things swell up.
explanation.walkthrough: "Swells" looks like a verb about swelling; it is the old noun for dandies. Labour is Britain's main left-wing party.
explanation.definitionFit: Swells and fops are both flashily dressed men of fashion.

clue.text: Dotty's through squeezing member!

indicators.note: the outer word squeezes the next inside

parts.note: by means through, as in by way of
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A saucy line about a woman called Dotty squeezing a member.
explanation.walkthrough: Dotty looks like a woman's name; it is the adjective meaning crazy. Barmy is British for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy and dotty both mean slightly mad.

clue.text: See 14ac.
Screw up by English university

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom

parts.note: lay is slang for screw, to have sex
E for English

explanation.surface: Someone making a mess of things because of an English university.
explanation.walkthrough: "Screw up" reads as a phrasal verb, to botch; it splits into screw, then up.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut.

clue.text: Puzzle lacking? Don't mention it!

definitions.meaning: a puzzle is a conundrum, and here there is none at all

explanation.surface: A modest reply to being thanked, with a hint that the task was easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally: an absence of any puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways to answer thanks, and literally the phrase means there is nothing to puzzle over.

clue.text: By which a celeb might get around making millions in fuel hike

definitions.text: By which a celeb might get around

indicators.note: the millions sit in the fuel, inside its letters
to hike is to hoist up, and in a down entry lifting letters reverses them

parts.note: oil is fuel
M for millions

explanation.surface: A star cashing in on a rise in fuel prices.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fuel hike" reads as a price rise; hike is the signal to lift the letters in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A limo, short for limousine, is the car a celebrity is driven around in.

clue.text: Forced Leeds, etc. to ditch candidate

indicators.note: the letters of the words are forced out of their order into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Leeds and other places are compelled to drop a parliamentary candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forced' rearranges the eight letters LEEDSETC.
explanation.definitionFit: To deselect is for a local party to drop its sitting MP or chosen candidate from standing again.

clue.text: Let's wave on having sex

parts.note: a perm puts waves in hair
it is slang for sex

explanation.surface: An invitation to wave goodbye to caution and have sex.
explanation.walkthrough: "Let's" looks like let us; here it is Let followed by the link 's.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to let someone do something is to allow it.
